It seems to me that the reason behind America's failed two party system, intense corruption, and stagnation is that nearly everyone believes that no matter what they do (writing their congressman, voting, etc) nothing will change. This idea perpetuates itself. How can we break this cycle? What must Americans, or indeed any country facing the same problem, do to change policy and direction?
How can we break the cyclic thinking that allows political apathy and corruption to thrive?

I honestly have recently come to the realization it isn't that political apathy is the root problem, it appears to be a symptom of the massive bureaucracy that exists in America. Which by itself is not a bad thing, but with the scale it is currently at means that voters are necessarily disenfranchised because there are way to many things being voted and talked about on the so many levels.

It almost does make more sense that various special interest groups, say a pro-environmental group, organizes and approaches the various boards and groups because ordinary people cannot have the time and resources to do so. This is how corruption has and will continue to have roots in American politics for sure though.

The best way to create massive political involvement, IMO, would be something like a mandatory app on American smart technology, that updates information on bills/acts/etc. that will be voted on within say a month, divided up by local, state, and national levels and make it a trend to discuss and have public polls on it. The main issue is that most bills shouldn't be decided upon by a mob rule things similar to the budget, or even the TPP but that's another beast in of itself.

Tl;dr (You should it's not long), Political apathy in America is created by lack of Time, Money, and Authority. Ideally we could use more transparency.

I've always felt that a more educated and intelligent society was the best route to bettering it. I don't just mean in terms of ability to repeat back certain facts in school. I mean this in a much broader scale with concepts that can be used to better change. Strive for more emphasis in teaching some of these values at every level (home, school, community, etc):

Personal Responsibility: While obviously not everyone is to blame for their problems, they are to blame if they're not trying to better themselves. Especially in an age where so many routes to knowledge and experience are open, no one wants to put in the effort themselves and are quick to give up in a defeatist attitude and blame others. So many opportunities are passed up on a daily basis that people don't even realize they could have had. Obviously exceptions apply, circumstances change, don't think I'm making blanket statements about any one section of a person or their life in particular.

Curiosity: The desire for knowledge. The desire for experience. The desire to push past the bottom line of a news story and explore cause, effect, alternative viewpoints, and the larger situation as a whole.

Open-mindedness: Eliminate bias when talking. View arguments more with the idea of didactics in mind instead of just trying to make the other person lose. Don't rush to repeat the same thing someone else has said. Embrace alternative viewpoints and don't disregard something someone says for any reason, whether they be a racist or believe in unicorns. Even evidence that are often taken to be fact can be flawed in their application or deceptive. Look deeper, stop giving in to cognitive bias. Entertain even the most extreme or outlandish ideas possible. You don't have to accept them. Nothing can simply be taken at face value to be true or false. Don't let your mind be predisposed to believing one side or another without proper consideration.

End predjudice: I mean this in regards to people who associate others with certain ideas. People can be a racist and still be worth hearing. People can think clouds are our imagination and still be worth hearing. Stop discarding opinions. Don't automatically assume that it's someone else's fault or that a certain social group is responsible. Don't automatically assume that any method of coercion is justifiable for past offenses. Give people the benefit of the doubt. Stop taking offense and using personal attacks. Argue against a person's argument, not against their character or irrelevant beliefs.

Think outside the box: Search for alternate methods. Be open to new possibilities. Don't just assume any one path is set or blame others for holding you back. Life does not follow a linear path. One thing will not necessarily lead to the next, and often times there will be detours and multiple routes able to be taken simultaneously. Just because it doesn't seem like it's in your immediate best interest doesn't mean it isn't worth doing.

I'm not sure if it's a common problem, but I have witnessed people stealing displays frequently. Those little decoy boxes you set out to show that you have a product, but you don't trust the customer enough to have it within their actual reach? The boxes that say DISPLAY all over them? Yeah, those...

My first experience with this problem was when I worked for an old video rental place before it went belly up. My manager had dealt with a few instances of kids stealing the video games, particularly the brand new ones, and finally decided we would keep all the game discs behind the counter in a folder and when they came to rent, we'd take the game out of the folder, put it in the case, and send them on their way. No more that a week after this change, we had this guy just randomly shove all the empty cases for the PS2 games into his coat and make a mad dash for the door. Manager and I share a meaningful look and then go about our evening. Said cases were all in the return box the next morning or soon after.

More recently was at my current place of employment, a veterinarian located inside a large retail pet store. We used to have a display tree on the front desk showing all the flea and tick and heartworm preventive products we sold and I'd written in sharpie DISPLAY all over them, because I'd gotten tired of people handing them to me and saying "I want to buy this". Gentleman walks in, says he has a question for the doctor. I ask him to relay it to me so that I can try and answer his question, turns out it is one I need to legitimately consult the vet about.
